look_here_first: CORM-BASED PANICGRASS (*Dichanthelium pedicellatum*): SEE ACTUAL attached fibrous roots and basal leaves in gallery panel 7 (Cody Stricker), with a source-connected but separate small green flowering spikelet panicle in panel 6 and fully leafy flowering stems in Bob Harms panels 8–9. The true cormlike swelling (~5×3 mm) is NOT clearly isolated on a measured same-plant root photo, and the SHORT 0.25–0.5 mm inner HAIR CURTAIN ligule is NOT the long, externally visible blade-edge cilia on Harms panel 12. Spindle/obovoid ripe spikelets ~3–3.5 mm, with two unequal glumes, require individual ruler-calibrated dissection for species-grade ID. THIS is not a winter basal-rosette grass. Do not misfile Cody photos as D. lindheimeri.

best_field_traits: Perennial with a shallow cormlike rooted base and cauline leaves; explicitly NOT basal-rosetted in Williamson County botanical treatment.
Vernal culms commonly have 4–7 thin stem leaves, often relatively narrow (approximately 1.3–5.5 mm broad in Central Texas treatment).
Upper leaf surface often finely hairy, underside much less hairy; margin and lower blade may carry a few long hairs with swollen bases.
True ligule often very short (~0.25–0.5 mm), requiring a macro view.
Open ovoid spring panicle; stalked/terminal obovoid spikelets roughly 3–3.5 mm.
Individual spikelets are awnless, with a lower sterile floret and fertile upper floret; precise glume characters need magnification.
crew_field_check: 1. Confirm original photo ROLE (flower macro, habitat view, or open panicle) before using a label; this image alone is NOT a verified same-plant key.
2. On a verified living shoot follow the stem down to its SMALL CORM-LIKE base with fibrous roots; do not teach a basal rosette as an identifying feature.
3. Open the collar: photograph true hair-fringe ligule separately from hairs at the blade base, with mm scale.

4. Measure at least three mature ripe SPIKELETS with 1-mm ruler; size categories ~1.3–1.6 lindheimeri, 2.1–3.2 commutatum, ~2.9–4 oligosanthes, ~3–3.5 pedicellatum, but overlapping ranges prohibit pure size-only identification.
5. If rosette/collar/leaf base or mature spikelet dimensions unavailable, record Dichanthelium sp. and a source-determined tentative species.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Connected small cormlike (up to 5 × 3 mm) base, fibrous roots and same-plant narrow cauline blades plus flowering shoot with mm/cm references.
0.25–0.5 mm hair-fringe TRUE ligule seen at a separated blade/sheath junction
Mature green oval spikelet of about 3–3.5 mm and glumes with mm reference
Whole spring panicle AND autumn leafy secondary shoot from same verified plant

confused_with: other Dichanthelium species (not yet represented in this learner)
comparisons.key_distinctions: Versus D. oligosanthes, 3–3.5 mm spikelet size overlaps; focus on genuinely narrow thin culm blades and a ~0.25–0.5 mm true collar hair fringe against oligosanthes' often longer 1–4 mm fringe. Lindheimer has tiny 1.3–1.6 mm spikelets; commutatum has broader often cordate stem blades and minute/absent ligule. Hair fringe must be viewed at scale, not inferred from isolated panicles.
comparisons.photo_context: Four real already archived source-labelled images are incorporated into a genus comparison. The Lindheimer habitat photo does not display a measured spikelet; none proves collar/leaf base anatomy. Morphological ranges are literature-based, not measured from these photographs.
not_reliable_alone: Airy panicle silhouette in a single season
Habitat or presumed annual/perennial condition from clipped stem
Ligule hair lengths or spikelet sizes inferred from photos without rulers
The older D. acuminatum var. lindheimeri name interpreted as a new separate species

field_id_finish_pass.crew_teaching_summary: Corm-based *D. pedicellatum* photo set now includes source-labelled actual fibrous roots and basal green culms (Cody 632024018), same-observation flowering spikelets and narrow leaf (Cody 632023937), Bob Harms complete aerial flowering habit, panicle, scaled attached spikelet and collar location. Achtung: collar photograph includes long BLADE-MARGIN hairs, not proof of true INNER ~0.25–0.5mm ligule. Genuine basal roots do NOT verify the 5x3mm cormlike swelling or attachment to same flower-bearing culm. Need measured corm/root/flower continuity, true inner hair curtain and dissected separated glumes and sterile/fertile florets; three look-alikes each retain own ID.
field_id_finish_pass.lookalike_comparison: Versus D. oligosanthes, 3–3.5 mm spikelet size overlaps; focus on genuinely narrow thin culm blades and a ~0.25–0.5 mm true collar hair fringe against oligosanthes' often longer 1–4 mm fringe. Lindheimer has tiny 1.3–1.6 mm spikelets; commutatum has broader often cordate stem blades and minute/absent ligule. Hair fringe must be viewed at scale, not inferred from isolated panicles.
photo_targets: REAL CORM: authenticate individual, expose actual shallow 5×3mm corm under basal sheath with all fibrous roots and attached flowering culm; photographed Cody root bundle is already useful but corm itself cannot be measured.

TRUE INNER HAIR LIGULE: fold blade and photograph inside collar at 10–40× with 1mm ruler, clearly separate 0.25–0.5mm short dense inner fringe from long blade-edge papillae and hairs seen in Harms collar picture.

SOURCE-ONE MATURE SPIKELET: 3–3.5mm ripe, authenticated, complete with lower glume / upper glume / lower sterile lemma / upper fertile lemma and palea individually separated and shown against mm scale.
MATCHED LOOK-ALIKES: D. oligosanthes and D. pedicellatum each rooted corm/caudex and opened inner ligule photos under the same camera scale; compare Lindheimer's much smaller actual ripe spikelets.

REUSE/SITE QA: retain original source photo individual license, check copyright/educational scope of five Bob Harms prior JPEG archives; inspect all 12 gallery panels and arrow overlays on mobile deployed Pages.

visual_comparison.subtitle: 8 true source-labelled species photographs + 1 historical illustration + 3 properly named look-alikes; actual roots in panel 7, no isolated measured corm or tiny true inner ligule.
visual_comparison.memory_rule: FIRST find the REAL fibrous-rooted base and look for a small cormlike swelling (not a basal rosette). SECOND show true INSIDE 0.25–0.5 mm HAIR FRINGE (not long blade-margin hairs). THIRD measure three ripe 3–3.5 mm obovoid spikelets. Lindheimer ~1.3–1.7, commutatum ~2.1–3.2, oligosanthes ~2.9–4 mm; substantial overlap needs morphology, not just numbers.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Corm-based pedicellate panicgrass — photograph actual roots, field habit, spikelet face, THEN open inner ligule
steps: START source-photo gallery panel 7 (index 6), Cody Stricker: Actual fibrous roots attached directly below living basal shoots. The tiny cormlike bulge is still not isolated with a 1mm ruler; never annotate one by inference.
Gallery panel 16 (index 15): a true living leafy flowering tuft in rocky Glen Rose field habitat. Foreground and surrounding grasses may overlap; neither buried roots nor individual corm are visible.

Gallery panels 13–14 (indices 12–13): real leaf–sheath insertion and some separate WHITE EXTERIOR HAIRS from Garner State Park and another Texas plant, shown to orient a true ligule search. These pictures do NOT show the opened tiny 0.25–0.5mm inner hair-curtain.

Gallery panels 15 & 17 (indices 14 &16): authenticated green intact oval *D. pedicellatum* spikelets, vein bands and fine marginal surface hairs; not detached glumes or fertile lemma. They contain NO millimeter ruler.

Gallery panel 10 (index 9) includes Bob Harms' existing ruler with attached spikelets, but not licensed under Creative Commons: reuse scope is credited scientific/educational only; do not relicense/reuse commercially.

COMPARISON index 3: real *D. lindheimeri* photographed with 1-mm bar by Dan Johnson; this is a DIFFERENT taxon with genuinely smaller spikelets than *D. pedicellatum* according to treatments. The two photographs have different scales and cannot be visually compared as if taken at identical magnification. Other comparison panels indices 2 and 4 are also OTHER species with original identity/licensing.
WHAT WE STILL NEED: photo of opened INSIDE of blade/sheath junction with 10× macro and 1-mm bar that isolates 0.25–0.5mm true ligular hairs from long exterior margin hairs.

After ligule, isolate the 5×3mm corm and show continuous attached plant shoots/roots. Then dissect measured ripe 3–3.5mm spikelet into lower/upper glumes, sterile lemma and fertile lemma at physical scale.

The three other CC BY research-grade originals with non-diagnostic views remain archived as source media but are omitted from the first-run Learner gallery. Historical line art is educational only and never counted as a photographed organ.
field_photo_quickcheck.field_rule: There is a crucial difference between a documented attached fibrous root system and a documented swollen subterranean corm; and between exterior collar hairs and the TRUE inner 0.25–0.5mm ligule. Verify with real scale.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: 16 real physically archived species JPEGs, one historical illustration, 3 true different-species comparisons; 17 gallery panels including 5 new high-value selected Texas CC BY photos, 11 new visible-only arrows, no new fake sub-mm labels. Relevant *D. lindheimeri* comparator now genuine 1-mm CC BY spikelet macro rather than the previously ambiguous mixed-grass CC BY-NC source. Conservative six-role =4.5/6 (75%). Taxon source still does not prove Hays county voucher; Pages deployment pending.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST
field_id_short_tiles.short: Actual fibrous roots photographed; cormlike swelling still unmeasured
field_id_short_tiles.details: Gallery panel 7 (index 6) is Cody Stricker's REAL rooted same-species plant: fine pale fibrous roots emerge from the basal sheaths and living green culms. This clears the ROOT ATTACHMENT evidence role. But the published shallow cormlike base (approximately 5×3 mm) is NOT cleanly exposed or measurable in these pixels; panel 6 (index 5), though in the SAME research-grade iNaturalist observation, does not prove physically continuous flowering culm to the rooted base. Use exact vouchered one-individual macro to establish actual corm size. Bob Harms index 7 shows aerial culms and flowering panicles, but no connected root.
field_id_short_tiles.status: ACTUAL ROOTS AND BASAL SHOOTS PHOTOGRAPHED — DISTINCT CORM AND FLOWERING LINK STILL MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 02 · OPEN THE TRUE COLLAR
field_id_short_tiles.details: Index 11 (panel 12) is actual Bob Harms source photo showing green blade–sheath junctions with clearly visible LONG blade-margin hairs. They do NOT substitute for the dense short (0.25–0.5 mm) FREE INNER ligule hairs reported in Williamson County treatment. Cody rooted habit (index 6) provides sheaths only, no opening of a true collar at microscope scale. A 1-mm physical bar and view from INSIDE the opened sheath are needed before a diagnostic hair-fringe arrow is placed.
field_id_short_tiles.status: TRUE COLLAR LOCATION AND LONG MARGIN HAIRS SHOWN — SHORT INNER LIGULE NOT PROVED

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 03 · FOLLOW LEAVES TO PANICLE
field_id_short_tiles.short: Narrow stem blades, open spring panicle
field_id_short_tiles.details: Bob Harms index 7 displays flowering leafy culms and entire small open panicles; index 8 shows multiple same-species panicle branches. Cody index 5 has a very useful bright green close flowering panicle against a hand with one true narrow leaf blade. Original iNat index 0 is another source-identified attached small spikelet/pedicel view. Never infer corm-to-panicle connection from separate photos without same-individual matching.
field_id_short_tiles.status: GROSS ATTACHED CULM AND PANICLE COVERED

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 04 · MEASURE MATURE SPIKELETS
field_id_short_tiles.details: Harms index 9 has a photographed scale beside actual obovoid spikelets on slender stalks, and index 10 provides flowering reproductive closer detail. Cody index 5 confirms similarly green attached spikelets, but hands/fingers are not 1-mm scientific rulers. Published mature length 3–3.5 mm and width 1.3–1.8 mm remain reported source ranges; the archival scale is useful but no individually isolated ripe spikelet has been calibrated and dissected here.
field_id_short_tiles.status: ACTUAL SCALED PANICLE/SPIKELET PLATE — ISOLATED MEASURED RIPE SPIKELET STILL NEEDED

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 05 · SEPARATE GLUMES AND LEMMAS
field_id_short_tiles.short: Lower/upper glumes and two florets: calibration and dissection still missing
field_id_short_tiles.details: Bob Harms indexes 9–10 show true source-labelled attached spikelets and scale, not separate glumes. Published lower glume about 1.5–2.1 mm, upper 2.5–2.8 mm; sterile lower and bisexual fertile upper florets lie WITHIN one complete spikelet. DO NOT arrow an unresolved glossy green margin as a measured glume/lemma or call a projecting flower organ an awn.
field_id_short_tiles.status: UNSEPARATED ORIGINAL SPIKELETS COVERED — GROSS DISSECTION STILL MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 06 · COMPARE CORM-BASED PANICGRASS AND ITS LOOK-ALIKES
field_id_short_tiles.short: Overlaps oligosanthes: use collar AND base
field_id_short_tiles.details: Three separately identified DIFFERENT species are panels 3–5 (indices 2–4): D. commutatum macro, D. lindheimeri scene, D. oligosanthes panicle. Exact D. pedicellatum own-source reproductive panels 6 and 10 (indices 5,9) and rooted crown index 6 help contrast the corm-based growth habit. Do not compare spikelet sizes from unscaled photos: *D. oligosanthes* overlaps 3–3.5 mm; actual root morphology and free inner ligule size needed. Two Cody Stricker photographs now stored in this CORRECT species card, not Lindheimer.
field_id_short_tiles.status: THREE CORRECT LOOK-ALIKES + ROOT AND FLOWER PHOTO LESSONS — MATCHED-SCALE DIFFERENCES MISSING
